messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGERDUTY: High severity incident triggered for service=redwood-hosted-inference, symptom=503/502 spikes from eu-west-3:az-c, impact=partial customer egress failures — paging oncall-ana :rotating_light:
oncall-ana: Seeing increased 502s for user-facing requests routed through az-c. Alert threshold at 5% now at ~18%. Can folks triage?
Alex K.: I'm on it. Starting with NAT/route checks for az-c subnets. Any recent deploys?
Priya C.: No deploys in the last 30m from product. Console shows spike at 02:07UTC.
Marcus R.: Reproducing: curl to a small handful of hosts in az-c returns 502 or hangs. Cross-region calls (eu-west-2 -> eu-west-3:az-c) show packet loss in traceroute.
Olivia S.: @Alex can you check route table propagation and if route table associations changed? We had an infra change earlier to automate propagation but I didn't see a push today.
oncall-ana: Alex, Priya — you're the primary responders. Marcus/Olivia assist. I'll update incident channel and start timeline.
Alex K.: Running aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=rw-azc-priv-rt
Alex K.: Found a route table (rtb-0a1b2c3d) that lost the route for 0.0.0.0/0 pointing to a nat-gateway in az-c. It shows propagated=false and association shows a different subnet id than expected.
Marcus R.: That matches traceroute. Looks like egress is blackholed for affected private subnets. Could be a route-assoc change or propagation lag. Any infra automation that touched associations?
Priya C.: Checking Terraform state and recent pipeline runs... nothing completed in last 12 hours. But infra ACL automation did a reconciliation yesterday.
Olivia S.: Can you dump the route table versions? Maybe a manual change by ops?
Alex K.: Putting the describe-route-tables output below:
```
{
  "RouteTables": [
    {
      "RouteTableId": "rtb-0a1b2c3d",
      "Associations": [ { "SubnetId": "subnet-aaa111", "Main": false } ],
      "Routes": [ { "DestinationCidrBlock": "0.0.0.0/0", "GatewayId": null, "NatGatewayId": null, "State": "blackhole" } ]
    }
  ]
}
```
Priya C.: State=blackhole means the target (nat-gateway) is missing/unhealthy or route references gone. Check nat-gateway status.
Marcus R.: aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --nat-gateway-ids nat-0abc1234 shows state "deleted" for nat-0abc1234 and a new NAT resource nat-0def5678 is in failed state. Timestamp of deletion ~1968889800 (a few mins before alert).
Olivia S.: Oof — was there automation for NAT rotation? I recall a script to tear down idle NATs. Might have mis-scoped.
Alex K.: Rolling mitigation options:
1) Re-associate affected subnets to a healthy route table with working NAT.
2) Recreate a NAT gateway in the AZ quickly (note: takes ~1-2 mins to allocate elastic IP + attach).
3) Switch outbound egress to a cross-AZ NAT in the same VPC as a temporary fix (update route to nat in az-b) — increases cross-AZ costs but buys time.
Which should we pursue in parallel?
oncall-ana: Do both 1 and 3 in parallel. Marcus, Olivia please prepare a new route table with a working NAT route. Priya, Alex create a NAT in az-c as plan B. I'll start customer communications.
Marcus R.: Creating temporary route table rtb-temp-azc and associating subnets subnet-aaa111 and subnet-bbb222. Command:
```
aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id vpc-12345 --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=route-table,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=temp-egress-azc}]'
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-temp-azc --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0xyztmp
aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id rtb-temp-azc --subnet-id subnet-aaa111
```
Alex K.: Creating NAT in az-c now: aws ec2 create-nat-gateway --subnet-id subnet-azc-nat --allocation-id eipalloc-xyz
Alex K.: NAT created nat-0new123 in pending. Will update when available.
Priya C.: Noted customer impact: ~12% of requests returning 502s, most of those in eu-west-3 region for workloads pinned to AZ-C. Escalating to SRE lead.
oncall-ana: Slack status updated: INCIDENT: EGRESS_FAILURE_EU-WEST-3_AZ-C — impact partial for hosted API, customers may see increased 5xx. Public status page updated to "degraded performance for eu-west-3".
infra-bot: runbook step: If nat-gateway deleted unexpectedly, create NAT + re-associate route tables or attach NAT instance in emergency mode — see /runbooks/vpc-egress.
Marcus R.: Temp route applied and associated to subnet-aaa111. Doing health checks.
Marcus R.: Validation: curl to endpoints now returns 200 from one test host — appears partial recovery. Still seeing some requests routed to older route table in other subnets.
Olivia S.: I'm patching the remaining subnet associations (subnet-ccc333, subnet-ddd444) to temp rt. Doing in small batches to avoid flapping.
Alex K.: NAT nat-0new123 is now "available". I will update temp route to point to real nat-0new123 and then decommission the broken references.
Alex K.: Updating route: aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-temp-azc --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0new123
Priya C.: Observability: error rate dropped from 18% to ~2.5% after the first associations. Latency normalized. Customers still affected in a few pods pinned to old route table.
Marcus R.: Completed remaining associations. Verified all subnets in az-c now point to temp-egr-rt with nat-0new123. System tests show success across samples.
oncall-ana: Good job. I'm going to change incident stage to "mitigated" and keep monitoring. Please record timeline and root cause hypotheses.
Olivia S.: Initial suspected cause: an automated cleanup job that removed an old NAT binding and deleted the nat-gateway resource without updating route tables — left some route tables referencing a now-deleted nat (blackhole). We'll need to audit automation and tighten IAM/tags.
Alex K.: Evidence: cloudtrail event at 1968889795 shows DeleteNatGateway called by role infra-cleanup-role from runner-executor-12.
Priya C.: Adding action items:
- Rollback/lockdown infra-cleanup job and add guardrails (tag check + approval)
- Create alert when route table state becomes blackhole for critical rtbs
- Postmortem and customer impact summary for status page
- Add e2e test for NAT rotation to avoid orphaned references
- Reconcile Terraform state for rtb-0a1b2c3d
Marcus R.: I'll draft runbook updates to prefer updating route tables before deleting NATs, and to use drain windows.
infra-bot: Incident checklist auto-populated: severity=P1, mitigated=true, followups_assigned=true.
oncall-ana: Handing incident to oncall-ana for postmortem follow-up. Thanks all — exceptional coordination.
Alex K.: Quick note: customers with pinned AZ routing (eg some enterprise Dedicated capacity) may have seen longer impact; we'll surface to account teams.
Priya C.: Last check: metrics stable for 12m. Closing alert channels; will leave incident open for postmortem.
Olivia S.: Adding owners to followups: infra-cleanup fix (Olivia), runbook updates (Marcus), alerts (Alex), postmortem writeup (Priya).
Marcus R.: I'll also open a ticket to scan for any other route tables referencing deleted NAT ids.
Priya C.: Thanks team. I'll run the postmortem template and ping customer success for outreach.
oncall-ana: Incident timeline saved. Changing Slack channel topic to "INCIDENT: mitigated — postmortem in progress" :white_check_mark:
